# Page

The Page surface: paints `--ds-surface` edge to edge with `--page-pad` (24) on every side and no radius, border, or shadow; children fill the content slot. Inside a Frame the Frame owns the pad and the Page adds none. A Page can carry its `title`: the page's one h1, at Heading/large 24, above the content. Sections inside it open at h2.

The content inside a Frame: a page header, then Sections on the 12-column grid. Three types: default, full width and reading.

Also asked as: surface.

## Usage

Use Page for the content of every default Frame. It carries the page header, the one h1, and the Sections under it. The default type caps the grid at 1232; full width is for a page that fills the window, such as chat, a board or a wide table; reading caps it at 864 for text people read through.

A Section shows its title row when the page, or the active page tab, holds several Sections, or when the Section has actions; the title then names the collection. A page or tab with one Section and no actions hides that Section's title (`isTitleHidden`). See Section.

## Motion

Page reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | Scroll to a spot on the page | `--ds-motion-linear` | The header is scroll-linked: the small title fades in at the end of the Breadcrumb row, its opacity mapped to the next 24 px of scroll. No spring, no timer, no snap when scrolling stops. |
| anchor | Scroll to a spot on the page | `--ds-motion-linear` | The actions and the tabs ride up with the page and anchor: the actions at the end of the Breadcrumb row, the tabs under it. One copy of every control. |
| tabs-shadow | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | The tabs' shadow appears when they stick, a single moment. In Reduced mode nothing changes: every movement is the person's own scroll. |

## Alternatives

- For one task that takes the whole window, use `Frame`.
- For a region of the page with its own heading, use `Section`.
- For one object with an agreed shape, use `Card` inside a Section.

## Best practices

### Make the page header the page's one h1. {#make-the-page-header-the-page-s-one-h1}

**Checked:** Automatic

A Section never stands in for it. Sections inside open at h2.

Do: The page header is the one h1; the Section under it opens at h2.
Don't: Sections standing in for the page title: two page-title-sized headings and no page header.

### Show the breadcrumb by the Navigation pattern. {#show-the-breadcrumb-by-the-navigation-pattern}

**Checked:** Review

When it shows and what it holds: the Navigation pattern.

Do: An area page: the title alone.
Don't: A breadcrumb on a top-level area page, repeating the Sidebar's place.

### Place page actions and the add action by the Navigation pattern. {#place-page-actions-and-the-add-action-by-the-navigation-pattern}

**Checked:** Review

Page actions sit at the end of the title row and are about the page only. Where an add action goes: the Navigation pattern.

Do: "Add" is the Section's one action, in its title row; the page header carries only page actions.
Don't: The same Primary twice: in the page header and in the Section's title row.

### Keep the description to one line. {#keep-the-description-to-one-line}

**Checked:** Review

Anything longer moves into the first Section.

Do: One detail line under the title.
Don't: A paragraph under the title pushes the first Section down.

### Keep one tab system per page. {#keep-one-tab-system-per-page}

**Checked:** Review

The rule and its reasons: the Navigation pattern. Page tabs name views of one subject; the Section under them has no views row, and a switch such as Status is a quick filter after Search.

Do: Under page tabs the Section has no views row; Status is a quick filter after Search.
Don't: Pill views under page tabs: two tab systems on one page.

### Shrink the scrolled header to one sticky row. {#shrink-the-scrolled-header-to-one-sticky-row}

**Checked:** Review

The breadcrumb with the title at its end, then the page actions; page tabs stick under it. The Section header rows scroll away. This state is planned.

### Show one banner at a time, scrolling with the content. {#show-one-banner-at-a-time-scrolling-with-the-content}

**Checked:** Review

Which tier a message belongs to: the Notifications pattern.

## Accessibility

- The Page is the `main` landmark. Its header's title is the one h1; Sections open at h2.
- The breadcrumb is a `nav` named "Breadcrumb".
- Page tabs are a tablist; the selected tab names its panel. Views swap in place and are announced.
- The StatusTag is text, never color alone.
- A title that truncates keeps its full text in a Tooltip on hover and focus.
- Text on a Page uses `--ds-text` at every level, in every color mode.

## Related

- Frame: use when deciding which type the page sits in.
- Section: use when a region needs its own heading, views or detail.
- Card: use when one object has a shape already agreed, or a checklist is built.
- Patterns: use when deciding where a breadcrumb or a tab belongs (Navigation), or choosing the StatusTag beside the title (Indicators).

Same group: `Card` · `Frame` · `Modal` · `Panel` · `Section` · `Table`

## Types

- **Default.** The content grid, centered and capped at its content width. Nearly every page.
- **Full width.** The content runs to the pad with no cap, for a page that fills it, such as chat, a board or a wide table.
- **Reading.** The grid capped at 864, the readable measure: training lessons, help articles and policies. A multi-step task and sign-in use it too.

The Frame's `width` sets the type: `default`, `full` or `reading`.

## Anatomy

A record page one level down shows every header slot, with markers in the gutter beside each part.

1. **Breadcrumb** (optional). The record's parents on their own row, above the title.
2. **Title.** The page's one h1, with its StatusTag after the text when the page is one record.
3. **Description** (optional). One line under the title.
4. **Page actions** (optional). At the end of the title row, about the page only.
5. **Page tabs** (optional). At the bottom of the header; they switch the whole page.
6. **Banner** (optional). Under the header, one at a time.
7. **Content.** Sections on the grid, under the header.

## Width behavior

Drag the width control. Above the content cap, content centers at the cap; below it, content fills the available width. The header keeps one h1 at every width.

## Key states

- **Page banner.** A message about this page sits under the page header and scrolls with the content. Which tier a message belongs to is the Notifications pattern, listed in the Patterns overview.

- **Header and banner slots.** Page owns the spacing from its header to the banner and content, including when the banner is removed.

## Slots

| Slot or prop | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `title` | The page's one h1, at the heading-xxl size, above the content. |
| `children` | The Sections and other page content. Existing pages may still supply the header and banner here. |
| `header` | One `PageHeader`: the h1 with `breadcrumbs` after a drill-in, `actions` and page tabs in `bottomBar`. Replaces `title`. |
| `description` · `status` | Planned. `PageHeader` has neither slot yet, so the examples here compose both in its `title` block: the `Heading`, a StatusTag after it, then one description line. |
| `banner` | One page `Banner`, below the header. Page separates the slots and content with `--page-stack-md`. |
| Type | Set on the Frame's `width`: `default` (1232), `full` (no cap) or `reading` (864). |
| Scrolled header | Planned. The sticky one-row header. |
| `as` | The container element. |

## Sizes

| Token | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| `--page-header-stack` | Between the breadcrumb, the title row and the page tabs. |
| `--page-header-gap` | Between the title and the page actions. |
| `--page-stack-md` | Header to the banner and the first Section; between Sections. |
| `--heading-xxl`, `--body-default`, `--body-sm` | The title, the description, the breadcrumb. |
| `--content-max-width`, `--content-max-width-reading`, `--content-min-width` | The default cap, the reading cap and the floor of the content grid. Full width has no cap. |
| `--grid-columns`, `--grid-gutter`, `--page-pad` | The 12-column grid, its gutter and the pad. |
| `--ds-surface` | The Page's one fill, with no shadow. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Title an area with what it holds, in sentence case: "Sessions". | Title case, or a title that repeats the breadcrumb. |
| Title a record with its name: "Maya Rodriguez". | "Student details". |
| One detail line: "Grade 8 · Math · Lincoln Middle School". | A paragraph under the title. |
| Page tab labels of one or two words: "Overview", "Sessions". | Numbered tabs, or tabs that wrap. |
